title: Guard proof: measure the fetch refspec, and quote git verbatim on fetch failure
description: Both findings arrived from opum-doc (ODOC-211, PR #301), which applied this repo's guard verbatim. Finding 1 is a defect in OUR proof that our own notes misdiagnosed: the OMARK-58 note reads the refspec mutant's survival as a bad-fixture artifact, but it survives the CORRECTED fixture too, for a different reason - with the refspec dropped, origin/dev is never created, so the rev-parse --verify split ONE STEP EARLIER fires, and its message carries the same THIS CHECKOUT IS SHALLOW / fetch-depth: 0 / exit 1 the shallow row asserts. Confirmed here by measurement, both variants on the same fixture. Finding 2 is the 2>/dev/null defect OMARK-58 recorded as known-unfixed with this exact prescribed fix.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The shallow row asserts the ABSENCE of the origin/dev-does-not-resolve wording, and dropping the fetch refspec dies with exactly 1 red - that row
scripts/ci/assert-main-fast-forward.sh line 38 drops 2>/dev/null, captures stderr and appends git verbatim; restoring the suppression dies with exactly 1 red
Clean tree fully green, and the other three mutants (assertion 1, 2, 3) still die, each predicted and named individually

finalSummary: Delivered in PR #120, CI run 35026221375 (step 'Promotion guard has a passing proof suite': passed 17, failed 0; all three required checks green on 31d92f4). Shallow row gained the absence assertion -"the fetch reported success but origin/dev still does not resolve"; the fetch dropped 2>/dev/null and now appends git verbatim with newlines flattened, asserted on 'git said: fatal:' rather than the unconditionally-printed stem. Mutation run, each predicted and named: assertion 1 -> DIED 5 red, assertion 2 -> DIED 1, assertion 3 -> DIED 3, drop refspec -> DIED 1 (SURVIVED 0 before), restore 2>/dev/null -> DIED 1. Both findings originated in opum-doc ODOC-211 and were confirmed here by measurement before being taken. The generalisable one: splitting the second missing-object site under OMARK-58 is what made the first one untested, so a fix that reroutes execution can move a property out from under its assertion - re-run mutants after a fix, not only before. Also corrected two comments carrying the superseded diagnosis. Still unproven and unchanged: the workflow wiring (BEFORE_SHA/FORCED from github.event), which stays open until this repo's first real promotion.
